analyst.summary: Bajaj Auto had a genuinely strong FY26 - motorcycle exports to Africa and Latin America are recovering fast as currency conditions there normalise, and its Chetak electric scooter has become a real, profitable #2 player in India's EV two-wheeler market behind TVS. But the stock's price already reflects all of this good news and then some: it trades near 27-29 times last year's profit, a level that assumes the export rebound, the EV lead, and the newly acquired KTM motorcycle business in Austria all keep delivering without a hitch. About a tenth of last year's reported profit growth actually came from a one-time accounting gain tied to the KTM acquisition rather than from selling more vehicles, and rising steel, copper and aluminium costs will pressure margins this year. We rate it a Sell on valuation grounds - a genuinely good company, priced for a best-case outcome that leaves little room for any of its growth engines to slow down.
